Implementation Plan

Implementation plan: authenticate Telegram tracking comments by author and exact body

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`
- `tests/test_tg_helpers_cleanup.py`
- `tests/test_tracking_comment_cap.py`
- `changelog.d/8598-tg-tracking-comment-author-trust.md` (new)

## Planning ref
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: `8e2b6e25e86751bec5cc71856b755c5b0b5ce6f1`, branch `orchestrator/project-8598`. Integration branch mismatch: false.
- The code the finding cites is in the committed copy of `scripts/tg_helpers.sh` on the integration branch (649 lines). `_tg_snapshot_tracking_entries` starts at line 263, the jq filters are at lines 298 and 301, and the DELETE calls are at lines 551 and 628. The checkout used for planning had an overlaid copy of the same file (512 lines, matching the default branch) that does not contain the snapshot helper. The implementer must edit the committed integration-branch version, which PR #8600 added (see `changelog.d/8600-tg-cleanup-snapshot-retain.md`).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _tg_snapshot_tracking_entries
Scope-mode justification: The finding asks for author-based trust and records that cannot span lines. The issue also says to fix every instance of the defect class. In `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`, four functions pick a tracking comment by its text alone and then act on it with the PAT:
- `_tg_snapshot_tracking_entries`, which feeds `tg_cleanup_msgs` and `tg_cleanup_phase_msgs` (DELETE).
- `tg_store_msg_id` and `tg_store_phase_msg_id`, which pick the newest marker-looking comment and PATCH it. A forged marker would make the bot edit someone else's comment and store real message IDs where cleanup will now ignore them.

The complete fix is one shared jq filter and one identity helper used by all four functions. That costs well under 30 extra lines compared with fixing only the snapshot, and it adds no dependency and no external interface. Under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete option wins. `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py`'s `_UNROUTED_PIPELINE_MARKER_RE` is left alone: it only stops a comment from counting as a human reply and never deletes or edits anything.

## Functions or modules to implement
All changes are in `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`. Indent with tabs and put opening braces on a new line, as the file already does.

1. **New `_tg_tracking_author_login`** returns the login of the identity that writes tracking comments. It reuses the repo's existing pattern of resolving the pipeline login from `/user` (`gh api user --jq .login`, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:51`). It uses this file's `curl_gh_api` so that it works without `gh` and with the existing curl fakes.
   - **Cache hit:** if `_TG_TRACKING_AUTHOR_LOGIN` is non-empty, print it and return 0.
   - **Lookup:** otherwise call `curl_gh_api -s --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: token ${GH_TOKEN}" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" "https://api.github.com/user"` and read `.login // empty` with jq.
   - **Validation:** require `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}$`, then lowercase it.
   - **Success:** cache the value in the global `_TG_TRACKING_AUTHOR_LOGIN` and print it.
   - **Failure:** on transport error, non-JSON, a missing login or a login that fails validation, print `github-actions[bot]` and return 0 without caching, so a later call retries. This is the `GITHUB_TOKEN` case: `/user` returns 403 for installation tokens, and those runs' comments are written by `github-actions[bot]`. The `secrets.GH_PAT || github.token` fallbacks in `implement.yml` and `orchestrate.yml` hit this case.
   - **Warning on failure:** emit one `::warning::Telegram tracking: could not resolve the GH_TOKEN identity; only github-actions[bot] tracking comments are trusted` to stderr. Never print the token or the response body.
   - **Batching note (§14):** a comment above the call records the audit. The comment-page reads do not return the caller's identity, and there is no existing cached login in this file. The cost is one call per process after the first success.

2. **New jq filter constant `_TG_TRACKING_JQ_DEFS`** (the name is not used anywhere in the repo). It is a jq `def` block that every selector uses:
   - **`trusted($login)`:** true when `.user|type=="object"`, `.user.login|type=="string"`, `.id|type=="number"` and `.body|type=="string"`, and either:
     - `$login != "github-actions[bot]"` and `(.user.login|ascii_downcase) == $login`, or
     - `$login == "github-actions[bot]"` and `.user.login == "github-actions[bot]"` and `.user.type == "Bot"`.
   - **`marker_ids($re)`:** returns `(.body | capture($re).ids)` or empty.
   - **Anchors:** every pattern uses `\A` and `\z`, not `^` and `$`. jq's Oniguruma treats `^` and `$` as line anchors, so a multi-line body would still match `^...$`.
   - **General pattern:** `\A<!-- tg_(?:cleanup|phase:[a-z_]+):(?<ids>[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]+)*) -->\z`
   - **Phase pattern:** `\A<!-- tg_phase:` + `$phase` + `:(?<ids>[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]+)*) -->\z`

3. **Change `_tg_snapshot_tracking_entries`** to take a third argument, `author_login`.
   - Keep each page only through `select(trusted($login))` and the anchored pattern.
   - Emit `"\(.id)\t\($ids)"`: the numeric comment id and the captured ID list only, never the body. Neither field can contain a tab or a newline, so a record cannot span lines.
   - If `author_login` is empty, return 1 with a `::warning::` (fail closed; callers delete nothing).
   - Keep the pagination, page cap, abort warnings and `__tg_snapshot_failed__` handling exactly as they are.
   - Update the header comment to describe the new record format and author rule.

4. **Change `tg_cleanup_phase_msgs` and `tg_cleanup_msgs`.**
   - Validate `phase` against `^[a-z_]+$` (phase cleanup only). If it fails, emit `::warning::` and return 0 with no API call, because `phase` is spliced into a regex.
   - Resolve `author_login="$(_tg_tracking_author_login)"` in the caller's shell before the snapshot subshell, so the cache survives, and pass it as the third argument.
   - Change the loop to `while IFS=$'\t' read -r comment_id id_list`:
     - Re-validate `[[ "${comment_id}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]` and `[[ "${id_list}" =~ ^[0-9]+(,[0-9]+)*$ ]]`, and `continue` (skip the record) on mismatch.
     - Remove the `sed -n` extraction from the comment body.
     - Keep the circuit breaker, the retention rule (BUG-006), the 10-second DELETE timeout and the warning text unchanged.
   - Every Telegram delete and GitHub comment DELETE then only reaches IDs from an exact marker written by the trusted identity.

5. **Change `tg_store_msg_id` and `tg_store_phase_msg_id`.**
   - Validate `phase` against `^[a-z_]+$` (phase store only). If it fails, return 0 with a warning.
   - Resolve `author_login` with the new helper.
   - Change the two jq selections (`tracking_id` and `tracking_body`) so they pick the last comment on the newest page that passes `trusted($login)` and the anchored marker pattern. The `sed` append stays the same and is now guaranteed to match.
   - Keep the fallback paths (create a new marker) unchanged. When no trusted marker exists, a new one is POSTed, as happens today when none exists.

## Data structures affected
- The snapshot's internal record changes from `comment_id<TAB>raw_body` to `comment_id<TAB>id_list`. Only `scripts/tg_helpers.sh` uses it. A search shows no other script or test calls `_tg_snapshot_tracking_entries`.
- Tracking comment bodies (`<!-- tg_cleanup:ids -->`, `<!-- tg_phase:PHASE:ids -->`) are unchanged.
- New process-global cache variable: `_TG_TRACKING_AUTHOR_LOGIN`.

## API or interface changes
- No public function signature changes: `tg_cleanup_msgs`, `tg_cleanup_phase_msgs`, `tg_store_msg_id`, `tg_store_phase_msg_id`, `tg_send_tracked`, `tg_send_phase_tracked` and `tg_delete_msg` are unchanged.
- The private `_tg_snapshot_tracking_entries` gains a required third argument.
- New GitHub API call: `GET https://api.github.com/user`, at most once per process after it succeeds.
- No new environment variables.

Failure modes:
- **`/user` fails** (installation token, rate limit, network). Symptom: one warning, and only `github-actions[bot]` markers are trusted. On a PAT run, the PAT's markers are skipped, so their comments and Telegram messages are kept and the next cleanup retries. Store POSTs a fresh marker. Recovery: the next process resolves the login.
- **A page read fails** during the snapshot. The existing behaviour stays: abort and delete nothing.
- **Forged or malformed marker** (wrong author, extra text, multi-line, non-numeric ids). The record is never emitted and never acted on. No warning is emitted, to avoid log noise from user comments.
- **Invalid phase argument.** Warning, no API calls, return 0.

## Decisions
### D1 — Trust tracking comments by author identity resolved from GH_TOKEN
- Chosen: compare `.user.login` (case-insensitive) with the token's own login from `GET /user`. Only when that lookup fails, trust `github-actions[bot]`, and only with `.user.type == "Bot"`.
- Alternatives considered: always trust both the resolved login and `github-actions[bot]`; trust by `author_association`; a new env var naming the bot login.
- Why: tracking comments are written with `GH_TOKEN`, so its identity is the only one that should be trusted. Repos set `GH_PAT` to a User-type account (the auto-answer on this issue comes from `@shubhodeep1`), so a "Bot only" rule would drop every real marker. Trusting `github-actions[bot]` only in the `github.token` fallback keeps the trusted set as small as possible. `author_association` lets any collaborator in, and a new env var adds configuration that can drift (§8 and §9).

### D2 — Emit only the extracted IDs, matched with absolute anchors
- Chosen: jq captures the IDs with `\A...\z` patterns and emits `id<TAB>ids`. Bash re-validates both fields.
- Alternatives considered: `@base64` the body and decode it in bash; keep
